item.content:encoded:
Sep 24, 2026, 11:33 AM ET
Across 102 innings (19 starts) in 2026, Houston Astros right-hander Hunter Brown has recorded a 6-3 record with a 3.26 ERA, 1.27 WHIP, and 120 strikeouts. The 28-year-old got off to a rough start to the year, missing over two months with a shoulder injury and posting a 4.94 ERA across 27 1/3 innings in July. However, Brown has begun to rediscover his top form in recent outings. Across his last 33 1/3 innings (six starts), Brown is 3-0 with a 2.43 ERA, 1.20 WHIP, and 48 strikeouts. Brown has had issues with command all year long, and his 11.9% walk rate has led to an elevated WHIP. However, he's boosted his strikeout rate all the way up to 28.1% and has struck out 39.1% of the batters he's faced across his first four starts of September. Heading into his final start of the regular season on Saturday against the Athletics, Brown is beginning to look like the fantasy ace he was drafted to be ahead of 2026.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
More Recent News
Sep 24, 2026, 11:21 AM ET
Across 501 plate appearances in 2026, Cleveland Guardians second baseman Travis Bazzana is hitting .245/.337/.404 with 15 home runs, 57 RBI, 53 runs scored, and 19 stolen bases. The 24-year-old's underlying batted-ball metrics are underwhelming, as he's logged just a 4.8% barrel rate and a 36.2% hard-hit rate. However, Bazzana's 11.2% walk rate is impressive for a young player and helps him get on base consistently and use his speed. Bazzana has also been red-hot of late, hitting .288 with six home runs, 15 RBI, and 11 runs scored across 69 plate appearances in September. If the former top prospect is starting to grow into his power, he could begin to emerge as one of the better second base options for fantasy managers. In leagues where he's on the waiver wire, Bazzana should be a priority target for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Sep 24, 2026, 11:15 AM ET
Across 655 plate appearances in 2026, Minnesota Twins first baseman Josh Bell is hitting .255/.317/.416 with 20 home runs, 92 RBI, 76 runs scored, and two stolen bases. The 34-year-old may not have one clear standout skill, but he remains a steady source of power and run production. Bell has kept his strikeout rate manageable at 19.9% while still posting solid barrel (9.5%) and hard-hit (42.0%) rates. The veteran switch-hitter also remains locked into everyday playing time in the heart of the Twins lineup, putting him in a good position to rack up runs and RBI. Heading into the final weekend of the regular season, Bell profiles as a balanced producer for fantasy managers to target on the waiver wire.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Sep 24, 2026, 11:10 AM ET
Across 444 plate appearances in 2026, Baltimore Orioles third baseman/first baseman Coby Mayo is hitting .225/.293/.463 with 24 home runs, 63 RBI, 63 runs scored, and four stolen bases. Swing-and-miss is the obvious red flag in Mayo's profile, as he's struck out in 30.2% of his plate appearances. However, the 24-year-old brings significant power upside with a 13.7% barrel rate and a 47.6% hard-hit rate. Mayo has hit .265 with 12 home runs since the All-Star break, and he's established himself as an everyday presence in the heart of the Baltimore lineup. For fantasy managers in need of power, Mayo profiles as a priority target on the waiver wire heading into the final weekend of the regular season.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Carlos Lagrange Could Join Yankees' Playoff Roster


Keith Hernandez




Sep 24, 2026, 12:02 AM ET
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone said that right-handed pitching prospect Carlos Lagrange is "in the conversation" for a spot on the team's postseason roster for the wild-card series next week against the division-rival Boston Red Sox, according to Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News. The 23-year-old Dominican is the team's No. 3 prospect at MLB Pipeline, and he has been ramping up his throwing program since coming off the seven-day injured list on Sept. 16 with a sprained right shoulder. Lagrange went 1-4 this year at Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, recording a 4.48 ERA, 1.35 WHIP, and 85:33 K:BB in 64 1/3 innings pitched across 19 appearances (11 starts). If Lagrange is pulled up to the Yankees' playoff roster, he would be making his major-league debut in the postseason in a relief role out of the bullpen. The 6-foot-7, 248-pounder has the tools to excel in high-leverage spots with an upper-90s fastball with armside run and multiple secondary pitches that can generate swings and misses consistently.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Daily News - Gary Phillips
Sep 23, 2026, 11:52 PM ET
Chicago Cubs right-hander Kevin Gausman (shoulder) came up wincing and in some apparent pain after diving to tag a runner out at third base during his start on Wednesday at Wrigley Field against the visiting Miami Marlins, according to Tony Andracki. Gausman was pulled from the game, but he was also at 101 pitches on the night. Manager Craig Counsell said that Gausman's left shoulder got extended awkwardly and "grabbed on him" on the play. He is now sore, and the Cubs will see how he feels in the next couple of days. Gausman is lined up to potentially start Game 1 or 2 next week in the wild-card series in the playoffs. The good news for the Cubs is that the injury is to the veteran's non-throwing arm as well. He came one out shy of a quality start for his fantasy managers on Wednesday, allowing two earned runs on six hits (one homer) while walking one and striking out seven in 5 2/3 frames for a no-decision. The 35-year-old veteran came into his final start of the regular season with a 9-12 record, 4.55 ERA, 1.27 WHIP, and 177 strikeouts in 172 innings pitched in 2026 with the Cubs and Toronto Blue Jays.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Tony Andracki
Sep 23, 2026, 10:59 PM ET
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone said that shortstop/second baseman Anthony Volpe could see some playing time at third base this week, per the Talkin' Yanks podcast. Volpe has mostly played shortstop in his MLB career, but he recently filled in at second base while Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. was sidelined by a thumb injury. With Chisholm Jr. back, it appears that New York could work Volpe into the mix at third base. The Yankees have gotten underwhelming production at the hot corner from Ryan McMahon, who has hit .210 with 11 home runs across 356 plate appearances in 2026. Volpe's numbers don't appear much better on the surface, as he's hit .244/.321/.335 with two home runs, 26 RBI, 24 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases across 234 plate appearances. However, the 25-year-old has been better in September, hitting .263 with four stolen bases across 40 trips to the plate this month.--Will Brady
Source: Talkin' Yanks
Chase Burns Working on Adding a Sinker


Will Brady




Sep 23, 2026, 10:47 PM ET
Cincinnati Reds starting pitcher Chase Burns (groin) was working on a sinker in his final starts before being placed on the 15-day injured list with a groin strain, per Charlie Goldsmith of the Charlie's Chalkboard Substack. Burns put together a dominant season in 2026, recording a 15-3 record with a 2.86 ERA, 1.17 WHIP, and 185 strikeouts across 154 1/3 innings (29 starts). However, Burns threw almost exclusively four-seam fastballs and sliders, mixing in the occasional changeup as well. Burns told Goldsmith that adding the sinker and continuing to develop his changeup should help him go deeper into games. If Burns can successfully add a sinker to his repertoire over the offseason, he could take his production to an even higher level in 2027.--Will Brady
Source: Charlie's Chalkboard - Charlie Goldsmith
Garrett Crochet Will Not Pitch this Week


Will Brady




Sep 23, 2026, 10:36 PM ET
Boston Red Sox left-hander Garrett Crochet (shoulder) will not appear in a regular-season game this week but is still in play to return during the postseason, per Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. Crochet is currently on the 60-day injured list and has not pitched since late April due to shoulder and lat issues. However, he's been working toward a return and could be a factor out of the bullpen for Boston at some point in the playoffs. While 2026 has been a lost year for the 27-year-old, Crochet was one of the best pitchers in baseball in 2025. Across 205 1/3 innings (32 starts), he recorded an 18-5 record with a 2.59 ERA, 1.03 WHIP, and 255 strikeouts. Crochet also has experience as a reliever, making 54 appearances out of the bullpen for the Chicago White Sox in 2021.--Will Brady
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Sep 23, 2026, 10:27 PM ET
Philadelphia Phillies starting pitcher Jesus Luzardo (shoulder) played catch for a fourth straight day on Wednesday and is expected to progress to mound work "very soon," per Matt Gelb of The Athletic. Luzardo has been sidelined since early September by shoulder inflammation, but it appears he has a chance to work out of the bullpen for the Phillies in the National League Wild Card Series. Across 178 2/3 innings (29 starts) before the injury, the 28-year-old recorded a 14-5 record with a 2.87 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, and 221 strikeouts. Luzardo posted a career-best 30.4% strikeout rate and an elite 23.2% K-BB rate. While the talented left-hander is unlikely to be fully built up as a starter, getting Luzardo back in any capacity would still be a major boost for Philadelphia.--Will Brady

Keith Hernandez




Sep 23, 2026, 3:22 PM ET
Boston Red Sox outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela (quadriceps) has been activated from the 10-day injured list on Wednesday and is in the starting lineup against the visiting Cleveland Guardians and left-hander Foster Griffin, starting in center field and batting sixth, according to Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. Rafaela is back for the tail end of the 2026 regular season after landing on the IL earlier this month with a strained right quad muscle. He did not go on a minor-league rehab assignment before returning, but instead took at-bats off a Trajekt machine. The Red Sox are hoping he will get enough at-bats in through the rest of the week to get him back up to speed for the start of the wild-card series next week against the division-rival New York Yankees. Rafaela is returning to a strong .282/.317/.443 slash line with a .760 OPS, 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 17 stolen bases, and 67 runs scored in his 535 at-bats this year. Boston is a much scarier team with their starting center fielder and power/speed threat back in time for the postseason.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Braves Reinstate Robert Suarez From Injured List


Keith Hernandez




Sep 23, 2026, 3:15 PM ET
The Atlanta Braves officially announced on Wednesday that they reinstated right-handed reliever Robert Suarez (elbow) from the 60-day injured list and optioned right-hander Owen Murphy to the minors in a corresponding move. After missing more than three months with inflammation in his right elbow, Suarez is back at the back end of the Braves' bullpen for the tail end of the regular season. The Braves might ease the 35-year-old veteran Venezuelan hurler back into the fold so that he is ready to roll for the postseason next month. Before his elbow injury, Suarez, a two-time All-Star who had 76 saves in the previous two seasons with the San Diego Padres, had been pitching extremely well in Atlanta. He was 4-0 with a 0.56 ERA (2.44 FIP), a 0.84 WHIP, four saves, 26 strikeouts, and six walks in 32 relief innings. Suarez's return definitely makes Atlanta's bullpen more intimidating, just in time for the postseason in October.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Atlanta Braves

item.description: Good morning, Chicago. ✶ 🔎 Below: Our investigation into the firing of a former principal now running for president of Chicago’s first-ever fully elected school board. 🗞️ Plus: A City Council recap, the push to save a mansion built by Mrs. O’Leary’s son, a new era for Chicago’s candy legacy and more news you need to know. 📝 Keeping score: The Cubs fell to the Marlins, 3-2; the White Sox lost to the Royals, 5-4. 🌤️ Today’s weather: Partly sunny with a high near 68. 📧 Subscribe: Get our morning ne
item.content:encoded:
Good morning, Chicago. ✶
🔎 Below: Our investigation into the firing of a former principal now running for president of Chicago’s first-ever fully elected school board.
🗞️ Plus: A City Council recap, the push to save a mansion built by Mrs. O’Leary’s son, a new era for Chicago’s candy legacy and more news you need to know.
📝 Keeping score: The Cubs fell to the Marlins, 3-2; the White Sox lost to the Royals, 5-4.
🌤️ Today’s weather: Partly sunny with a high near 68.
📧 Subscribe: Get our morning newsletter delivered to your inbox weekday mornings.
⏱️: An 8-minute read
TODAY’S TOP STORY 🔎
Reporting by Mila Koumpilova and Sarah Karp
Biggs banned: Jessica Biggs claims leading a South Side school is a top reason voters should pick her in the race for Chicago’s first elected school board president. That’s even though she was fired from her job as principal of Burke Elementary in 2018, and until recently, was banned from working in Chicago Public Schools.
Candidates’ claims: Biggs, a current school board member, has maintained she was terminated based on a rushed internal investigation after openly criticizing district practices. Her opponents say her dismissal revealed a deliberate, multi-year scheme to falsify attendance data to game her school’s rating.
Our investigation: A WBEZ and Chalkbeat Chicago investigation shows a more nuanced picture. At Biggs’ direction, Burke staff improperly marked students tardy. An uptick in the school’s attendance rate helped improve a high-stakes rating given to the school. But the inspector general’s report does not lay out a full-blown conspiracy to cheat, and it’s hard to say how much of the attendance bump came from mislabeling students versus a concerted effort to get kids to school.
Meet the candidates: Attorney Victor Henderson, leadership consultant Sendhil Revuluri, and former Chicago Teachers Union deputy political director Hilario Dominguez also want the president’s seat. Learn more about them here.
CITY COUNCIL RECAP 🏛️
Reporting by Fran Spielman
Vote delayed: Mayoral allies temporarily derailed an ordinance at Wednesday’s City Council meeting that would require future borrowing to be approved by a three-fifths vote. That’s 30 votes instead of the current benchmark of 26.
Data center decision: Also on Wednesday, Mayor Brandon Johnson followed through on his promise to propose a one-year moratorium on new or expanded data centers until permanent regulations are established to mitigate their impact on the power grid, the water supply and the environment.
TIF approved: Additionally, Council members authorized a $201 million tax increment financing subsidy to pave the way for JDL Development to start construction of the first phase of Foundry Park, a $3 billion replacement for the failed Lincoln Yards mega-project.
Settlements OK’d: A nearly $14 million settlement was approved to compensate two defendants framed by corrupt Chicago Police Detective Reynaldo Guevara for murders they said they didn’t commit. A $6 million payout to the family of a man killed in a police chase was also OK’d.
Meter deal update: On Thursday, a parking meter compromise is up for a vote in the Council’s Finance Committee.
CHICAGO HISTORY ✶
Reporting by Lee Bey
Historic mansion: An endangered Englewood mansion built by the Victorian-era man-about-town and gambler James “Big Jim” O’Leary — his mother and her cow were blamed for starting the Great Chicago Fire — should be granted preliminary landmark status, the city’s two leading preservation groups said Monday.
Key context: The vacant, 125-year-old O’Leary Mansion, 726 W. Garfield Blvd., is currently in demolition court under a raft of code violations. The three-story, 33-room house was designed by Zachary Taylor Davis, an architect whose works include Wrigley Field and the old Comiskey Park.
Status case: “We’re looking at a number of factors [as reasons to landmark the house], from the architecture to the architect, to the people connected with this place,” Landmarks Illinois Interim President and CEO Frank Butterfield said.
MORE NEWS YOU NEED 🗞️
- Funeral home scandal: A hearing is scheduled Thursday in a lawsuit against South Chicago Chapel, the funeral home where 56 decomposing bodies were discovered in August. Here’s what to know.
- 3rd person charged in man’s death: An 18-year-old man appeared in court Wednesday, marking the third suspect charged in the homicide of Kyle Bickham, who was pushed off a Red Line train Sept. 7.
- Tylenol murders lead: A man who died in 1982 could have ties to the Tylenol murders case, according to law enforcement in Idaho. Dr. Matthew Francis Betkouski hasn’t been named a suspect, but his former coworkers reportedly accused him of claiming he could commit the “perfect crime” by slipping poison into pharmaceuticals.
- Misconduct hearing set: The judge who uncovered apparent misconduct by prosecutors in the “Broadview Six” conspiracy case has scheduled a hearing Oct. 1 to help her decide what to do about the discovery that shook the Dirksen Federal Courthouse this summer.
- Chicago extends Divvy contract: The network of rentable bikes, e-bikes and scooters is planning some changes, including discounted pricing on the South and West Sides and a new bike model.
- Joffrey doc: A new PBS documentary captures the discipline, creativity and heart behind the Joffrey Ballet’s trailblazing “Winning Works” program for emerging artists historically excluded from ballet.
ON WBEZ 91.5 FM 📻
- Bridgeport’s concerns: Residents Jonathan Chen and Maria LaGiglio explain how they’re viewing Amtrak’s plan to move its Chicago maintenance facility from South Loop to Bridgeport.
- Card conversations: Jordan Abell, a Chicago high school senior behind a new card game inspiring debate, joins the show to discuss.
- Manopause: Men’s hormones and testosterone levels can change as they age. A medical expert and callers weigh in.
CHICAGO MINI CROSSWORD 🌭
Today’s clue: 3D: Like the cuisine at 88 Marketplace
FROM THE PRESS BOX ⚾🏈🏀
- Remembering Don Cooper: A former White Sox pitching coach who led a World Series-winning rotation, Mr. Cooper died at age 70.
- Bregman recovering: The Cubs’ Alex Bregman said Wednesday that he “felt like I got hit by a baseball bat to the face,” and he’s working to make a quick return.
- Williams unphased: Bears QB Caleb Williams is back to being a punching bag, but he’s never let a little backlash get him down, writes Jason Lieser.
- High school boys basketball: There have been many changes to high school basketball in the last several years — Joe Henricksen breaks them down.
BRIGHT ONE 🔆
Reporting by Maggie Hennessy
More than a century after Wrigley, Brach’s and Mars helped turn Chicago into a candy epicenter, a trio of artists with an unabashed candy obsession brought their gummy candy startup to the shuttered former Jelly Belly plant in suburban North Chicago, ushering in a new era for this storied city of sweets production.
The actor Martin Starr and musicians and twins Ezra and Adeev Potash cofounded Sweet Stash last fall with an additive-free gummy with the complex flavor and texture dimension of candies they discovered over years of globe-trekking.
“We are obsessed with candy beyond what’s normal and maybe even healthy,” Ezra said.
After months of routinely selling out on Amazon amid requests from retailers for their toothsome, musical note-shaped Jams gummies in flavors like Prickly Pear, Strawbarb and White Peach, the company moved production from Nebraska (the twins’ home state) to Ferrara’s 113-year-old Jelly Belly factory in April.
The move doesn’t just mean taking on bigger orders and getting onto more indie store shelves while maintaining consistency in a product free from gluten, synthetic dyes and corn syrup. This self-starting trio can also keep making candy limited mostly by their imaginations in a city known for confectionery innovation — a rarity for an industry dominated by profit-seeking conglomerates.
“We’re a small band of creative people going up against billion-dollar companies that make candy by the tank,” Adeev said.
YOUR DAILY QUESTION ☕️
Aside from the ballpark, where’s the next best place to watch a Cubs or White Sox game? Tell us what makes that place the best.
Reply to this question via email (please include your first and last name). We may run your answer in a future newsletter or story.
PICTURE CHICAGO 📸
Thanks for reading the Sun-Times Morning Edition!
Got a story you think we missed? Email us here.
Written and curated by: Matt Moore
Editor: Michael Lansu

item.content:encoded:
We’re down to the final days of the 2026 regular season with still quite a number of teams that have something to play for -- including a few who are fighting for their postseason lives.
Such is the case with the Astros and Rangers, who are tied atop the AL West (with Houston owning the tiebreaker); the team that loses the division will most likely miss the playoffs entirely. Elsewhere in the American League, the Guardians and White Sox are still battling for the division title, though the loser of that should slot into the third wild-card spot.
While all the divisions in the National League have been clinched already, the wild-card race, specifically in terms of seeding, is very much heating up, with the Phillies, Cubs and Padres entering play on Wednesday in a three-way tie.
Which clubs will get to keep playing into October? And which will watch their playoff aspirations come to an end?
Our expert panel has ranked every team based on a combination of what we’ve seen so far and what we already knew going into the 162-game marathon that is a full baseball season. We also asked ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle, Buster Olney and Jorge Castillo to weigh in with an observation for all 30 teams.
1. Milwaukee Brewers
Record: 99-59
Previous ranking: 1
With the season down to a handful of games, the Brewers have all but run out of time for Kyle Harrison to recover his first-half form. Harrison was 8-2 with a 3.01 ERA before the break; he’s 2-3 with a 7.80 ERA since. His strikeout rate has remained steady, even as his velocity and movement measures have become more volatile. Meanwhile, his walk rate has more than doubled, and his homers-allowed rate has nearly tripled. Suffice to say, this is not a great combination of trends. Milwaukee has tried to get Harrison back in stride by using him out of the bullpen, but he’s gotten hammered as a reliever. Brewers fans who dreamed of a big three rotation of Jacob Misiorowski, Harrison and Logan Henderson probably need to recalibrate their expectations at this point. -- Doolittle
2. Los Angeles Dodgers
Record: 97-61
Previous ranking: 2
We’re nearing October baseball, and it’s as if the Dodgers are knocking off items on a to-do list. Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup? Check. Edwin Diaz finding his stuff, finally? Check. Will Smith back in the lineup? Check -- and he has an OPS of close to 1.000 this month. Mookie Betts back to being Mookie Betts? Check. Kyle Tucker digging out of his seasonlong slump? Check. L.A. is putting the pieces back together just in time as it begins its effort to become the first NL team to go back-to-back-to-back. -- Olney
3. Tampa Bay Rays
Record: 96-62
Previous ranking: 3
Tampa Bay began the season with the longest odds to win the AL East. On Tuesday, it clinched its first division title since 2021 with a win over the Yankees. The Rays will enter their first postseason since 2023 as the favorites to win the AL pennant behind a distinct home-field advantage at Tropicana Field, a strong pitching staff and a dynamic lineup centered around MVP candidate Junior Caminero, designated hitter Yandy Diaz and first baseman Jonathan Aranda. With a payroll that ranks 28th in the majors, the Rays seek to become the team with the lowest-ranked payroll to ever win the World Series. -- Castillo
4. Atlanta Braves
Record: 93-65
Previous ranking: 5
Atlanta would’ve preferred to get a first-round bye in the playoffs, of course, but the fact that the Brewers and Dodgers seemed to have locked down the No. 1 and No. 2 seeds allows the Braves to treat this last week of the regular season like the last week of spring training. They can plot out the best way to rest their key relievers, assess the progress of Robert Suarez and arrange at-bats for the position players to be primed for the postseason. Meanwhile, the teams the Braves are likely to face in the first round -- the Phillies, Cubs and Padres -- are all still pushing for berths and home-field advantage in the wild-card round. -- Olney
5. New York Yankees
Record: 91-67
Previous ranking: 4
Despite manager Aaron Boone saying on Tuesday that Aaron Judge isn’t expected to return from his calf strain in time for the wild-card round, Judge told ESPN the following day that he does in fact intend to be ready for Game 1. He suffered the injury last Wednesday and was placed on the injured list two days later. The Yankees were initially cryptic about the setback, declining to disclose the severity and Judge’s outlook.
Boone offered some clarity Tuesday when he called it a “moderate strain” and acknowledged that the club does not plan on having him to open the postseason. Judge received a PPP injection Monday. The Yankees hope that will spur recovery. Otherwise, New York faces an uphill challenge to survive in October without its three-time MVP at his best. -- Castillo
6. Chicago Cubs
Record: 87-71
Previous ranking: 6
No player has made more of a second-half leap than Alex Bregman, whose season has just gathered momentum almost daily since the last week of July. That momentum was stopped in its tracks when Bregman suffered facial fractures last weekend when struck by a foul ball. The good news is that the Cubs decided against placing Bregman on the IL, believing he might be ready for the playoffs after.
But even if that proves to be optimistic, Cubs fans can take solace in the presence of icy-cool rookie Pedro Ramirez. The Cubs didn’t drop off much when Dansby Swanson was injured, as Ramirez provided a league-average bat and glove work at both second and third base that has kept an elite Cubs defense on track. You want Bregman in there, for sure -- but Ramirez provides a heck of a Plan B. -- Doolittle
7. San Diego Padres
Record: 88-70
Previous ranking: 8
San Diego’s magic number for clinching a playoff spot is shrinking, allowing general manager A.J. Preller and skipper Craig Stammen the chance to line up their staff for the wild-card series, with options developing. Stammen indicated to reporters that unless Michael King is needed to clinch a playoff spot on the last day of the regular season, he will be held over to start Game 1 of the wild card, wherever that is -- so he wouldn’t necessarily be used Sunday in order to win home-field advantage in the first round of the playoffs.
Additionally, the Padres are in a better position to rest their bullpen, the perceived strength of the team. Adrian Morejon ranks third among all relievers in innings. Rest might be overrated for Mason Miller: He has made 16 appearances on zero days’ rest, and in those games, he has allowed two hits and one earned run in 16⅔ innings, with two walks and 27 strikeouts. -- Olney
8. Philadelphia Phillies
Record: 87-71
Previous ranking: 7
The culture of Philadelphia’s starting pitchers, from Zack Wheeler to Cristopher Sanchez to Aaron Nola, is to pitch deep into games. Unlike so many starters in this generation, Wheeler takes the mound expecting to work into the late innings -- and the Phillies will need this sort of production from the rotation, given the team’s recent bullpen problems. Orion Kerkering, an important part of the relief corps, struggled so badly that he was sent to the minors last week. Jose Alvarado has pitched better down the stretch, and hard-throwing Alex MacFarlane has quickly ascended into an important role in his rookie season in the bullpen. But the Phillies’ rotation will carry the team’s October dreams. -- Olney
9. Boston Red Sox
Record: 85-73
Previous ranking: 9
The Red Sox rewarded Chad Tracy on Tuesday for leading the team’s historic turnaround by removing his interim tag and giving him a three-year contract to continue as manager. Now he’ll look to accomplish what his predecessor Alex Cora couldn’t last year: beating the Yankees on the road in the AL Wild Card Series.
Boston has cooled off since going 32-5 to put itself in playoff position and faces some injury uncertainty going into October. Ceddanne Rafaela returned Tuesday after missing 16 games with a quad injury, and Willson Contreras was hit by a pitch on his right hand last Thursday and is dealing with soreness. On the mound, the Red Sox could receive two significant reinforcements for the bullpen in Garrett Crochet and Tanner Houck. Crochet, last season’s AL Cy Young runner-up, has been out with a shoulder injury since late April, while Houck hasn’t appeared in a game in 2026. -- Castillo
10. Cleveland Guardians
Record: 82-76
Previous ranking: 12
Cleveland is, once again, showing its knack for a strong finishing kick. Over the past decade, only the Dodgers have won more September games. For Guardians fans aching for their team’s first title since the Truman administration, October is a higher priority at this point.
Like the White Sox, the first order of business is to secure the AL Central title and the first-round bye likely to go with it. Given the neck-and-neck nature of Cleveland’s battle with Chicago, there likely isn’t going to be much time for manager Stephen Vogt to ease up on the pedal to finish the season. That would be nice to do when it comes to rookie ace Parker Messick, who will finish the season with at least 50 more innings than he has ever thrown in a season. Messick has shown no signs of fatigue, so it may not matter. -- Doolittle
11. Arizona Diamondbacks
Record: 84-74
Previous ranking: 10
Manager Torey Lovullo’s comments in a radio interview last week in which he acknowledged that the Diamondbacks “probably” -- his word -- need to reach the postseason to earn him a contract extension surprised many in the industry, as Lovullo has a strong and long-standing relationship with his boss, Mike Hazen. The Ketel Marte situation has been challenging for the organization, with the team’s highest-paid position player failing to show up to the park, and owner Ken Kendrick has a reputation for being mercurial and demanding. Lovullo’s contract runs out at season’s end, and he and the Diamondbacks agreed they would discuss his status then. -- Olney
12. Chicago White Sox
Record: 81-77
Previous ranking: 11
The White Sox have wobbled down the stretch, but they have not fallen down. It looks like they will join the playoff party, completing an incredible two-year turnaround that saw them go from setting the modern single-season loss record to playing in October.
Barring a face-plant over the last few days of the season, the question of whether the Sox can overtake Cleveland for the AL Central title is the biggest remaining question. It’s impactful, with a first-round bye likely on the line. A bye is a boon for any team, but among likely postseason entrants, it might loom largest for the White Sox. That’s just because of how manager Will Venable has had to stretch his pitching resources to the maximum just to get to this point. A wild-card skip would give his staff at least a little time to regroup before the ALDS begins. -- Doolittle
13. Pittsburgh Pirates
Record: 80-78
Previous ranking: 14
Why did Paul Skenes lapse into baseball’s pitching middle class rather than continue his march toward Cooperstown? There is no bigger task for the Pirates and Skenes this offseason than figuring this out. With one more start to go, he has already allowed more runs this season than he did in his first two seasons combined. To be sure, it’s not all on Skenes, whose expected ERA, 3.27 per Statcast, is unusually divergent from his actual ERA (3.91). Still, even a 3.27 ERA is a far cry from the level of effectiveness Skenes flashed before this season. Why? Finding the answer to that question could prove to be the biggest addition Pittsburgh makes this winter. -- Doolittle
14. Texas Rangers
Record: 78-80
Previous ranking: 16
With eyes on the disappointing Mariners and Yordan Alvarez’s Triple Crown watch, the Rangers quietly remained in contention in the historically dreadful AL West all summer. Following three straight losses, they now find themselves tied atop the division with Houston. Texas will host the Mets in a series finale Thursday before finishing the season with three games in Minnesota. The Rangers will need to finish with a better record than the Astros, who own the tiebreaker, to reach the postseason for the first time since winning the 2023 World Series. -- Castillo
15. Houston Astros
Record: 78-80
Previous ranking: 13
The Astros fired general manager Dana Brown last month and are under .500 with four games remaining ... but they still have a real chance to win the division. That’s the AL West in 2026. The Astros finish the regular season with a four-game series in West Sacramento against an A’s team that has an MLB-worst run differential. The bad news: The Astros head there tied atop the division. The good news: They hold the tiebreaker over Texas. In the background over the last few days of the season: Alvarez’s push to become the first player to win a Triple Crown since Miguel Cabrera in 2013. -- Castillo
16. Toronto Blue Jays
Record: 77-82
Previous ranking: 15
The Blue Jays did not replicate their 2025 magic in 2026, largely due to injuries and their offense falling off a cliff. They finished last season fourth in the majors with a 112 wRC+; this season, they’re tied for 24th with a 95 wRC+. The dropoff starts with Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and George Springer. Guerrero has nine home runs -- and, inexplicably, just one at home -- with a .695 OPS in the first year of a 14-year, $500 million contract extension. Springer, who reversed a precipitous decline to hit 32 home runs with a .959 OPS last season, has 15 home runs with a .730 OPS in 124 games this year -- and he’s a free agent after this season. Whether Springer re-signs or not, a rebound in 2027 starts with Guerrero sparking an offense that is tied for last in home runs in 2026. -- Castillo
17. Miami Marlins
Record: 78-80
Previous ranking: 18
Here’s the good news about the Marlins’ 2026 season: They hung around all year, battling among the contenders and having some individual successes. Here’s what’s not-so-great about where they stand right now: It’s hard to identify the players who could lead a Miami breakout into full-scale contention with the best NL teams.
Otto Lopez had an excellent season, but he’ll turn 28 years old next week and his OPS is under .800. Griffin Conine is the one player on the team with an OPS over .800, and he’s 29. Sandy Alcantara reestablished himself as a rotation leader, but he’s 31. Eury Perez has flashes of dominance and is just 23, but he’s got an injury history and will finish this season with an ERA over 4.00. More depth and more talent is needed for the Marlins to take the next step. -- Olney
18. Baltimore Orioles
Record: 78-81
Previous ranking: 19
Another disappointing season in Baltimore has already prompted some changes in the front office, but not at the top. President of baseball operations Mike Elias is expected to return in 2027. One move his front office got right was signing Pete Alonso last winter. The first baseman, who has played in every game this season, hit his 40th home run of the season in Monday’s win over the Blue Jays. He clearly isn’t why the Orioles aren’t going to the postseason for the second straight year.
Baltimore’s young position player core has not lived up to the hype, while the pitching staff wasn’t good enough to shoulder the load. Elias & Co. already decided to move on from former No. 1 pick Adley Rutschman, an All-Star catcher previously considered a foundational player, at the trade deadline. More significant moves could come this offseason. -- Castillo
19. St. Louis Cardinals
Record: 77-81
Previous ranking: 17
This rebuilding season has been an unqualified success for the Cardinals. If not for a leaky bullpen, their soft wild-card contention might have been a lot more solid. While bullpens are sometimes the final piece of the contention puzzle for a building team, that’s not always the case. Some clubs develop a bullpen-building process that takes effect even as the rest of the roster remains a work in progress. The Pirates of recent vintage are a good example.
Thus, the project of putting together a contention-worthy bullpen is a crucial one for the Chaim Bloom-led front office. Bloom was part of a Rays front office that annually churned out elite, no-name bullpens. However, during the four years that Bloom led the Red Sox front office, Boston ranked 24th in bullpen ERA (4.48) and middle-of-the-pack in save percentage. Good first year, but there is more to prove in St. Louis. -- Doolittle
20. Detroit Tigers
Record: 74-85
Previous ranking: 20
The Tigers will probably finish fourth in the AL in run differential, perhaps third if they pass the Red Sox, and will easily pace the Central by that measure. When you consider that, along with Detroit’s freakishly bad record in one- and two-run games (now 21-51) and the relatively short list of players on expiring deals (Jack Flaherty and Gleyber Torres, along with the retiring Justin Verlander), the Tigers are an obvious and very strong bounce-back candidate for the 2027 season. That doesn’t mean that president of baseball operations Scott Harris and his staff don’t have their work cut out for them when it comes to evaluating this lackluster season. Still, for the Tigers’ disappointed fans, it’s important to keep in mind that their team will be proceeding from a relative position of strength. -- Doolittle
21. Washington Nationals
Record: 75-84
Previous ranking: 23
In so many ways, the 2026 season was a success for the Nationals, who exceeded expectations this year, flirting with contention in the first half and seeing the development of players like CJ Abrams and James Wood into offensive stars. But the team’s pitching collapsed in the second half -- Washington’s second-half ERA of 4.49 ranks 25th. The Nationals locked down Cade Cavalli to a multiyear deal last week at the end of what has been a breakout season, but it’s clear that president of baseball operations Paul Toboni’s greatest challenge is to develop the sort of pipeline of pitching that will allow them to compete with the big-market teams in the division. -- Olney
22. Seattle Mariners
Record: 74-84
Previous ranking: 24
A year after falling one win short of the franchise’s first World Series appearance, the Mariners’ season will end Sunday with a whimper. The 2026 campaign will be remembered as the most disappointing one in franchise history.
Cal Raleigh’s drop-off from 60 home runs and an MVP runner-up finish was baffling. Julio Rodriguez regressed and still hasn’t made the superstar jump widely expected of him. Josh Naylor was a below-average hitter in the first year of his five-year contract. The starting rotation was not as good as advertised. Changes are inevitable, likely starting with manager Dan Wilson. But the Mariners can’t fire all of their players. They’ll need their core to bounce back from down seasons in order to rebound in 2027. -- Castillo
23. New York Mets
Record: 73-85
Previous ranking: 21
No one will go into the 2027 season under more pressure than David Stearns, the Mets’ head of baseball operations, following their collapse down the stretch in 2025 and the poor 2026 season. So it makes sense that he worked to keep someone he has a working relationship with in the managerial role, Andy Green, who had his interim tag removed and was hired to a three-year deal Tuesday. Steve Cohen’s comments on an SNY broadcast about needing new voices within the organization got the attention of a lot of rival executives, who wondered if the impact of Pete Alonso’s encore performance at Citi Field and the “Fire Stearns” chants last week made an impression on the owner. Under the circumstances, hiring Green seems like the right move for Stearns, the smart move. -- Olney
24. Minnesota Twins
Record: 75-84
Previous ranking: 22
The arrival of prospects Kaelen Culpepper, Walker Jenkins and Emmanuel Rodriguez has the Twins’ prospective 2027 position group in good shape even if veteran Josh Bell declines his mutual option and departs. The murkiest position is catcher, where Ryan Jeffers is likely headed for free agency, presumably after the Twins issue him a qualifying offer. The QO could limit Jeffers’ market, but probably not that much, as Jeffers looks like the best free agent catcher option out there. If he leaves, the Twins will need someone to pair with Caratini.
Long term, after drafting Vahn Lackey third in the most recent draft, the Twins seem in good shape with him, Eduardo Tait, Khadim Diaw and Carson Tinney all showing well in prospect rankings. Alas, none of that quartet is likely to be a 2027 solution. -- Doolittle
25. Cincinnati Reds
Record: 73-85
Previous ranking: 25
The ongoing maturation of Elly De La Cruz, as he edges toward his career prime, has provided ample reason to keep an eye on the Reds, even amid a last-place showing. Still, there have been enough trade rumors regarding the supremely talented shortstop to make you wonder just how long De La Cruz will be around.
Recent comments made by his agent, Scott Boras, don’t help. Boras suggested to reporters that a future foray into the open market made more sense for De La Cruz than a below-market extension. What does that mean for the Reds in the near term? For now, he has three more years of team control, so there’s no reason to be rash. Still, with this cloud starting to form over Great American Park, some sort of clarity about how the Reds plan to deal with their best player would be nice. -- Doolittle
26. Kansas City Royals
Record: 68-90
Previous ranking: 26
The Royals’ biggest offseason project will be to figure out their 2027 bullpen formula. That process begins with evaluating the relievers already on hand. Presumed closer Carlos Estevez had shoulder surgery -- bafflingly not until the second week of September -- and the Royals almost certainly won’t pick up their 2027 club option on him. Lucas Erceg looked lost before being shipped off to Omaha, but he performed well in Triple-A and his velocity upon his return to the majors has been at its highest level all year. Which Erceg is the real one? Is journeyman righty Nate Pearson a leverage option? Does Craig Kimbrel have anything left? The Royals will need relief help from outside the organization, but how much of it will depend on the outcome of these evaluations and others. -- Doolittle
27. San Francisco Giants
Record: 65-94
Previous ranking: 27
The general perception of San Francisco’s farm system is that it improved in 2026, and Bryce Eldridge established himself as a player the organization could build around. Beyond that, however, the Giants really haven’t progressed. They have a top-heavy payroll situation, with hundreds of millions owed to Rafael Devers, Willy Adames and Matt Chapman. The questions about manager Tony Vitello making the jump from college to professional baseball weren’t quelled by his first season with the Giants -- and neither were the questions about the man who hired him, Buster Posey, who is still relatively new to his front office role. -- Olney
28. Athletics
Record: 63-95
Previous ranking: 28
The A’s are stumbling to the finish line having lost 95 games. All-Star catcher Shea Langeliers recently returned from knee surgery, but several other prominent players remain on the IL, including Nick Kurtz, Tyler Soderstrom, Jacob Wilson, Brent Rooker, Luis Severino and Gage Jump. They’ll enter their season-ending series against the Astros with a negative-217 run differential -- the worst in the majors by 33 runs. With one season remaining before the A’s move to Las Vegas in 2028, they enter the winter in search of a general manager after David Forst’s departure in early August. Their offseason priorities are straightforward: Get healthy and improve a pitching staff that has a 5.43 ERA (29th) despite pitching half its games at the launchpad known as Sutter Health Park. -- Castillo
29. Los Angeles Angels
Record: 60-98
Previous ranking: 29
The Angels, despite 11 straight losing seasons, are the only franchise in the majors that has yet to post a 100-loss season. That could change this weekend in Seattle, where the Angels will need to win three of four games to avoid reaching the century mark. It’d be a fitting conclusion to Arte Moreno’s tenure as owner. Last month, Moreno agreed to sell controlling interest in the team to Stan Kroenke for a record valuation of $4 billion. Kroenke will take over a franchise that has not appeared in the postseason since 2014 and has not won a postseason game since 2009.
The first order of business this offseason will be hiring fired general manager Perry Minasian’s replacement. The team could also be in search of a manager to replace Kurt Suzuki, who is on a one-year contract. It is a transformative time in Anaheim. -- Castillo
30. Colorado Rockies
Record: 57-101
Previous ranking: 30
Colorado has compiled 100 losses for the fourth consecutive season; the last team to suffer 100-plus losses in five consecutive seasons were the Phillies, from 1938 to 1942. In Paul DePodesta’s first year of running Colorado’s baseball operations, there were some under-the-hood improvements: the biggest run differential improvement of all 30 teams in 2026, an improved farm system and some nice finds for the every-day lineup, like Jake McCarthy, TJ Rumfield and Connor Norby. There’s still a long way to go to competitive relevance for the Rockies, especially given the high bar required in the Dodgers’ NL West. -- Olney

item.title: [Claro Sports] Chris Sale vuelve a desafiar la historia: consigue su novena temporada con 200 ponches y entra a un grupo exclusivo en Grandes Ligas
item.dc:creator: Juan Carlos Campos Rodríguez
item.description: El lanzador de los Atlanta Braves alcanzó una cifra histórica y reafirmó su dominio desde la lomita a sus 37 años Chris Sale volvió a colocar su nombre entre los grandes lanzadores de las Grandes Ligas. El zurdo de los Atlanta Braves alcanzó la cifra de 200 ponches en una temporada por novena ocasión en su carrera, un registro que lo coloca dentro de un grupo exclusivo en la historia reciente de MLB. El serpentinero consiguió la marca al ponchar a 10 bateadores durante la victoria de este miérco
item.content:encoded:
El lanzador de los Atlanta Braves alcanzó una cifra histórica y reafirmó su dominio desde la lomita a sus 37 años
Chris Sale volvió a colocar su nombre entre los grandes lanzadores de las Grandes Ligas. El zurdo de los Atlanta Braves alcanzó la cifra de 200 ponches en una temporada por novena ocasión en su carrera, un registro que lo coloca dentro de un grupo exclusivo en la historia reciente de MLB.
El serpentinero consiguió la marca al ponchar a 10 bateadores durante la victoria de este miércoles 23 de septiembre por walk-off de los Bravos por 3-2 ante los Cincinnati Reds en el Truist Parkla y reafirmó una de las características que han definido su trayectoria: su capacidad para dominar a los bateadores mediante la potencia de su recta, su slider y una mecánica que durante años lo convirtió en uno de los lanzadores más difíciles de enfrentar.
Además, Sale se unió a Randy Johnson como los únicos lanzadores zurdos en la historia de MLB con nueve o más campañas superando los 200 ponches. La lista de pitchers con más temporadas de este tipo está encabezada por Nolan Ryan, con 15, seguido por Randy Johnson, con 13, Roger Clemens, con 12, y Tom Seaver, con 10.
Además de su cifra de ponches, el veterano cerró la temporada regular con una efectividad de 2.16, uno de los mejores registros entre los lanzadores calificados de MLB. Solamente Jacob Misiorowski (1.86) y Cam Schlittler (1.94) presentan mejores números entre quienes cumplen con los requisitos estadísticos.
Su campaña también lo coloca dentro de la historia de los Braves. Desde 1920, únicamente Greg Maddux —con efectividades de 1.56 en 1994 y 1.63 en 1995—, Reynaldo López —1.99 en 2024— y Warren Spahn —2.10 en 1953— habían registrado una efectividad de 2.16 o menor en al menos 25 aperturas durante una temporada con la franquicia.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Pete Alonso busca una marca histórica que nadie ha conseguido en 106 años de Grandes Ligas
Chris Sale vuelve a alcanzar una cifra histórica
La temporada con 200 ponches representa un nuevo capítulo en la carrera de Sale, quien alcanzó esta cifra por primera vez en 2012, cuando todavía pertenecía a los Chicago White Sox.
Desde entonces, el lanzador mantuvo una notable regularidad como especialista en ponchar rivales. Sus registros le permitieron superar nuevamente la barrera de los 200 abanicados en múltiples campañas con los White Sox, Boston Red Sox y ahora Atlanta Braves.
La marca confirma la trayectoria de un pitcher que ha enfrentado diferentes etapas dentro de MLB, incluidos periodos marcados por lesiones, pero que logró mantenerse como una referencia cuando estuvo disponible sobre la lomita.
Un dominio que se mantiene con el paso de los años
Chris Sale ha construido su reputación sobre su capacidad para generar swings fallidos y limitar la producción ofensiva de sus rivales. A lo largo de su carrera se ha caracterizado por mantener altos niveles de ponches y una presencia constante entre los lanzadores más destacados de la liga.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Alex Bregman recibe pelotazo en el rostro y abandona juego de Cubs
El zurdo explicó la importancia de mantenerse enfocado durante una temporada larga y destacó el trabajo colectivo detrás de sus resultados. “No lo haces solo. Es un esfuerzo de todos los días, de preparación, de trabajo y de tener la confianza de tus compañeros”, señaló Sale sobre el camino que lo llevó nuevamente a alcanzar una cifra histórica.
Su consistencia también le permitió sumar reconocimientos individuales, como el Premio Cy Young de la Liga Nacional en 2024, además de múltiples apariciones en el Juego de Estrellas.
Sale mantiene la potencia de su brazo rumbo a los playoffs
Más allá de los números, Sale demostró que su velocidad y capacidad de dominio siguen vigentes. En su última apertura de temporada regular, su recta de cuatro costuras alcanzó un promedio de 97.8 millas por hora, una de sus mejores marcas con ese lanzamiento como abridor desde 2018. Además, realizó cuatro lanzamientos que superaron las 99.5 millas por hora, una muestra de que su brazo mantiene la potencia pese al paso de los años.
El siguiente reto para Sale será la postemporada. El lanzador está programado para abrir el primer juego de la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Nacional ante los Padres, donde buscará trasladar su dominio de la temporada regular al escenario más importante de MLB.
A sus 37 años, Chris Sale continúa agregando capítulos a una carrera marcada por los ponches, los reconocimientos individuales y ahora una nueva marca histórica que lo coloca junto a algunos de los mejores lanzadores zurdos en la historia de las Grandes Ligas.

item.title: [chicago.suntimes.com] Alex Bregman ‘felt like I got hit by a baseball bat to the face,’ working to make quick return to Cubs
item.dc:creator: Vinnie Duber
item.description: Trust me, you don’t want to be Alex Bregman right now. “I felt like I got hit by a baseball bat to the face, pretty much,” the Cubs’ third baseman said Wednesday, three days after he took a foul ball to the face while standing on deck during a game in Cincinnati. Bregman and the Cubs have said they’ve received relative “great news” since, in terms of a potential return, one that could come as soon as this weekend. But while that would be a boost to the Cubs’ chances as they approach the most mea
item.content:encoded:
Trust me, you don’t want to be Alex Bregman right now.
“I felt like I got hit by a baseball bat to the face, pretty much,” the Cubs’ third baseman said Wednesday, three days after he took a foul ball to the face while standing on deck during a game in Cincinnati.
Bregman and the Cubs have said they’ve received relative “great news” since, in terms of a potential return, one that could come as soon as this weekend.
But while that would be a boost to the Cubs’ chances as they approach the most meaningful games of their season, he’s dealing with some significant aftereffects, with multiple facial fractures.
“The pain’s been fine,” Bregman said. “I guess I fractured something right by the nerve in my face, so the whole left side of my face has been a little bit numb. As soon as the swelling goes down, I’m sure I’ll feel the breaks a little bit more.
“But all in all, I’m super lucky that it hit where it hit. A lot of gratitude, because if it was a few centimeters higher, it could have been detrimental.”
And here’s some more body horror:
“There’s a lot of fluid in my face,” Bregman said. “If I move, the fluid moves. If I’m bouncing up and down, my face feels like it’s bouncing up and down.”
All that is to illustrate what Bregman’s dealing with. But being the lauded hard-worker he is, it’s little surprise that he’s champing at the bit to get back in the lineup.
“[Tuesday] was brutal. I wanted to play,” he said. “I hope [to play this weekend]. We’ll see. One step at a time. I don’t know. I’m going to try to get in there [Wednesday].”
That last line was a joke, in case you were wondering. Bregman still has a lot to test out to see how he feels and how realistic such a quick comeback is.
“He’s doing well. But we’ve got to take some steps here,” manager Craig Counsell said. “I’m excited how he feels, and he’s excited. But he still needs to feel some things. He hasn’t run around yet, and he’s got to do that. He’s got to know what it feels like.
“We’ve got to be careful, and we’ve got to go through the proper steps.”
Bummer of a bunt
Utility man Matt Shaw entered Wednesday with a .176 batting average in his last 18 games.
He got a chance to help produce a run in extra innings Tuesday, but he popped up a bunt attempt with two men on and nobody out in the 10th inning of an eventual 8-2 loss.
It’s a relative nit to pick from a game in which the Cubs went 1-for-18 with runners in scoring position, but with a lot on the line in the season’s final week, it could be among the moments that loom large.
“These are the moments you prepare for,” Shaw said. “I know that I’m going to have a situation again where I’m going to have to put a bunt down. We all know what the stakes are. All we can do is keep preparing for these moments.
“An experience like this is going to help the next time I’m in that situation, and that’s all you can walk away with.”
Palencia back?
Since allowing seven runs in his first five outings after a lengthy IL stint, righty reliever Daniel Palencia hasn’t allowed an earned run in seven straight appearances, helpful as the Cubs look for their bullpen to stabilize before the postseason begins.

item.title: [fansided.com] Alex Bregman doesn't look like a guy ready to play a Cubs Wild Card series game
item.dc:creator: Chris Landers
item.description: Chicago Cubs fans around the country breathed a sigh of relief on Tuesday, when manager Craig Counsell sure made it sound like the team didn't expect Alex Bregman's ugly facial fracture to keep him out of the team's postseason lineup. In fact, Counsell went as far as to say the third baseman could be back in Chicago's lineup as early as this weekend. Just 24 hours later, though ... well, let's just say we have our doubts. Wednesday afternoon brought an interview with the man himself, and while B
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs fans around the country breathed a sigh of relief on Tuesday, when manager Craig Counsell sure made it sound like the team didn't expect Alex Bregman's ugly facial fracture to keep him out of the team's postseason lineup. In fact, Counsell went as far as to say the third baseman could be back in Chicago's lineup as early as this weekend.
Just 24 hours later, though ... well, let's just say we have our doubts. Wednesday afternoon brought an interview with the man himself, and while Bregman is grinning and bearing it as best he can, it's hard not to read between the lines here and wonder how exactly he'll be ready to play playoff baseball in a matter of days.
Bregman spoke to ESPN's Jesse Rogers prior to the Cubs' game against Miami, describing the fracture as "something by the nerve of my face" — adding that, as the swelling goes down, the actual fractures have become more and more painful. He did say that the pain was "fine," but, well, that's exactly what you'd expect someone of Bregman's track record to say. In reality, you need to see pretty well to hit a baseball, and even if Bregman does insist on toughing it out in October, you have to wonder what version of him Chicago will be getting.
Cubs fans probably shouldn't get their hopes up after Alex Bregman's latest injury update
From the "never a thing you want to hear an athlete say" department, Bregman also told Rogers that fluid build-up in his face is affecting him.
In a word: yikes. Again, Bregman is as tough a player as there is in the league, and he'll no doubt do everything in his power to be in the lineup when the Cubs kick off their Wild Card series (opponent TBD) next Tuesday. And to be sure, his face already visually looks a whole lot better than it did just 48 hours or so ago; give it another few days, and the swelling and bruising should subside even more.
All of which fails to reckon with the fact that Bregman has a broken bone in his face. Not just in his face, but awfully close to his left eye, the one closest to the pitcher as he steps in the box as a right-handed hitter. Less swelling is still some swelling, and there's still the pain — and, apparently, the fluids — to worry about. It seems almost unfair to expect Bregman to hit at anything like his usual level if he's having a hard time focusing on the baseball, and that should have the Cubs thinking long and hard about whether he belongs in the lineup.
Projected Cubs lineup if Alex Bregman misses Wild Card series
Of course, it's easy for me to say, and much tougher for Craig Counsell to actually execute. Not only is Bregman a veteran leader with a great deal of latitude, but his absence would leave a notable hole in the Cubs lineup.
| Player | Position |
|---|---|
| Pete Crow-Armstrong | CF |
| Seiya Suzuki | RF |
| Michael Busch | 1B |
| Ian Happ | LF |
| Nico Hoerner | 2B |
| Michael Conforto | DH |
| Dansby Swanson | SS |
| Pedro Ramirez | 3B |
| Carson Kelly | C |
Pedro Ramirez and Matt Shaw are both exciting, versatile young players, but installing them as an every-day third baseman for a playoff series feels like asking a lot. Both are just league-average hitters, and because of Bregman's iron-man tendencies, neither has a ton of third-base experience this year (though Shaw played there a bunch last season).
Chicago does have plenty of firepower around them, in the form of pending NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong, Seiya Suzuki, Michael Busch and others. But Bregman has been scorching hot for pretty much the entire second half, and losing his bat would be a devastating blow to a lineup that would suddenly start to look pretty top-heavy — especially with Dansby Swanson just making his way back from an oblique injury.

item.title: [Newsday] Cubs' Bregman on the mend after getting struck in the face by a foul ball

Sporting a discolored left eye after being struck by a foul ball in the on-deck circle Sunday, the three-time All-Star said it could’ve been worse. “Super lucky it hit where it hit and just a lot of gratitude that it wasn’t a few centimeters higher,” he said before Wednesday night’s game against Miami. item.content:encoded:
CHICAGO — Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman is thankful he’s not a little shorter.
Sporting a discolored left eye after being struck by a foul ball in the on-deck circle Sunday, the three-time All-Star said it could’ve been worse.
“Super lucky it hit where it hit and just a lot of gratitude that it wasn’t a few centimeters higher,” he said before Wednesday night’s game against Miami.
The ball, off the bat of teammate Michael Busch n Cincinnati, caused several facial fractures.
With the postseason approaching, the Cubs are glad the injury won’t require a stint on the injured list.
Bregman said he’ll likely start shagging ground balls in a day or so and will be trying out new styles of helmets to protect the eye.
“The whole left side of my face has been a little bit numb,” he said.
The Cubs can clinch an NL wild-card berth with a win Wednesday night or an Arizona loss.
“He’s still got significant swelling in his face and his eye that needs to improve,” Chicago manager Craig Counsell said Tuesday. “But all things considered, he’s in a good place.”
Bregman was on deck in the fourth inning of a 9-1 win at Cincinnati when he was hit on the left side of his face by Busch’s check-swing foul. Bregman immediately jogged toward the Cubs’ dugout and covered his face before going back to the clubhouse with an athletic trainer.
“When everything was going down on Sunday afternoon, I think that we all thought the worst case might be a possibility,” president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer said Tuesday. “And all the news since then has been really good. He’s had a lot of different doctor’s appointments, and they’ve been positive. And I think we have to take it one step at a time.”
Bregman is batting .262 with 26 homers and 89 RBIs in 153 games during his first season with Chicago. He signed a $175 million, five-year contract with the Cubs in free agency.
The 32-year-old Bregman got off to a rough start in his new home, hitting just .229 with two homers in his first 20 games. But he has been one of Chicago’s most productive players since the All-Star break, batting .305 with 17 homers and 48 RBIs in his last 57 games.
Bregman also has excelled in the postseason in the past. He won two World Series championships with the Houston Astros. He appeared in at least two postseason games in each of the previous nine years.

item.content:encoded:
CHICAGO — Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman could play again in the regular season after he sustained multiple facial fractures when he was struck in the face by a foul ball.
Chicago manager Craig Counsell said Bregman did a light workout in the weight room and tracked pitches from a machine in a batting cage. There are no plans to place him on the injured list.
"He's still got significant swelling in his face and his eye that needs to improve," Counsell said. "But all things considered, he's in a good place."
Bregman was on deck in the fourth inning of a 9-1 win at Cincinnati when he was hit on the left side of his face on Michael Busch's check-swing foul ball. Bregman immediately jogged toward the Cubs' dugout and covered his face before going back to the clubhouse with an athletic trainer.
"When everything was going down on Sunday afternoon, I think that we all thought the worst case might be a possibility," president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer said. "And all the news since then has been really good. He's had a lot of different doctor's appointments, and they've been positive. And I think we have to take it one step at a time."
Pedro Ramírez started at third in an 8-2 loss to Miami in 12 innings. He went 0 for 5 with two strikeouts. Matt Shaw also could fill in at third while Bregman is out.
Chicago (87-70) can clinch an NL wild card with a win over Miami or a loss by Arizona at Colorado.
The Cubs have five games left in the regular season. But the schedule for their weekend series at Boston is in flux because of heavy rain in the forecast.
"I think Alex is going to be fine. I really do," Counsell said. "The guy is ... he's driving home from Cincinnati and he wants to play. So he's planning on playing. He knew he had to get some good news from the doctors. He got that good news. So he's going to do everything in his power, and as long as I think symptoms don't kind of increase or happen as he increases activity, I think you're going to see him play."
Bregman is batting .262 with 26 homers and 89 RBIs in 153 games during his first season with Chicago. The three-time All-Star signed a five-year, $175 million contract with the Cubs in free agency.
The 32-year-old Bregman got off to a rough start in his new home, hitting just .229 with two homers in his first 20 games. But he has been one of Chicago's most productive players since the All-Star break, batting .305 with 17 homers and 48 RBIs in his last 57 games.
Bregman also has excelled in the postseason in the past. He won two World Series championships with the Houston Astros. He appeared in at least two postseason games in each of the previous nine years.
"To see a friend and a teammate just get hit in the face and bleeding like that is awful," Cubs second baseman Nico Hoerner said. "I think his reactions to everything has been uplifting, just him being relentlessly aggressive and positive and speaking out, all the things that he's excited to do."

item.title: [FanSided] MLB Rumors: Marcelo Mayer's Red Sox anger and Don Mattingly's Phillies future
item.dc:creator: Chris Landers
item.description: It's not the trade that will have the most bearing on who wins the World Series this fall, but the Boston Red Sox' decision to dump former top prospect Marcelo Mayer onto the San Francisco Giants stands out as among the most quietly curious of this past deadline. Then again, hearing Mayer and his family speak about his time in Boston ahead of his debut with his new team, perhaps it was for the best all the way around. Will Mayer be able to prove that the Red Sox got this one wrong? The latest ro
item.content:encoded:
It's not the trade that will have the most bearing on who wins the World Series this fall, but the Boston Red Sox' decision to dump former top prospect Marcelo Mayer onto the San Francisco Giants stands out as among the most quietly curious of this past deadline. Then again, hearing Mayer and his family speak about his time in Boston ahead of his debut with his new team, perhaps it was for the best all the way around.
Will Mayer be able to prove that the Red Sox got this one wrong? The latest round of MLB rumors has more on that as well as the Philadelphia Phillies' looming Don Mattingly decision and Alex Bregman on the mend for the Chicago Cubs.
Marcelo Mayer and his family sound relieved to be out of Boston
Not all that long ago, Mayer was a crucial part of the future for the Red Sox, as much a foundational prospect as Roman Anthony. But he struggled to stay healthy over the last two years, and struggled to hit even when he was in the lineup. Eventually, Boston decided they'd seen enough, flipping the young infielder to San Francisco at this year's trade deadline — and it seems as though Mayer is eager to prove that Craig Breslow was wrong to cut bait.
According to Susan Slusser of the San Francisco Chronicle, Mayer and his family "let the Red Sox front office know they'd be comfortable with a trade" as the atmosphere in Boston grew hostile toward the 23-year-old.
“Obviously, it didn’t go the way I wanted,” Mayer told Slusser, “and obviously, outside the lines, it’s a lot over there.”
Mayer's dad was willing to go even further, saying that he "jumped 30 feet in the air" when he heard the news that his son was headed back to his home state of California.
On the one hand, Mayer's offensive numbers over his first two big-league seasons are undeniably ugly, and he's missed time due to injury in each of the past four years. Then again, none those health issues seem to be of the chronic variety, and they undoubtedly hampered his development. You can understand why the Red Sox weren't willing to wait around for Mayer to maybe turn into a big-league second baseman, but you can also understand why the Giants were eager to give him a second chance — and why, given all the criticism he faced from fans and talk-radio types in Boston about whether he was soft, Mayer can't wait to get back on the field.
Phillies waiting until offseason to make a decision about Don Mattingly
It's been a big few days for interim managers, with both Chad Tracy in Boston and Andy Green with the Mets earning the full-time job moving forward. But no such vote of confidence has come for Phillies interim skipper Don Mattingly, who took over from Rob Thomson back in late April and has guided the team to the brink of a Wild Card spot. And from the sound of it, he shouldn't get his hopes up.
"[We] have felt it is better to wait until our season is complete," Phillies president Dave Dombrowski told reporters this week, per Scott Lauber of the Inquirer.
That seems to be a pretty clear warning: Take this team deep into October, or else. And really, despite Mattingly's 78-51 record at the helm this season, it's hard to fault Dombrowski too much here. The roster Mattingly inherited certainly has its flaws, with a thin bullpen and a lineup with multiple trouble spots. But Mattingly also hasn't helped matters at times, with some questionable decision-making that makes clear why his previous managerial stints ended unhappily.
Yes, he deserves credit for his role in Philly's turnaround. But it has much more to do with the players on the field than anything else, and the Phillies are wise not to tie themselves to a 65-year-old who could very well come back to bite the team in the postseason. And if Mattingly does prove himself next month, they can very easily revisit the matter.
Cubs appear to have dodged a bullet with Alex Bregman injury
The Cubs suffered a real scare in Cincinnati over the weekend, when star third baseman Alex Bregman took a line drive directly to the face while standing in the on-deck circle. Given the frightening nature of the injury and the timing just a week before the end of the regular season, it was hard not to fear that Chicago might have to at least begin its playoff journey without a guy who's been one of their very best players in the second half.
Thankfully, though, the Cubs appear to have gotten good news. Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures in the incident, but manager Craig Counsell told reporters on Tuesday that the veteran isn't expected to go on the IL — and that he might even be able to return to the lineup before the regular season concludes.
Will Bregman be the same guy he was prior to the injury? That remains to be seen. But as things stand right now, it seems like he'll at the very least be ready to go for the Cubs' first postseason game next week, and that's a huge sigh of relief.

item.content:encoded:
Sep 23, 2026, 11:45 AM ET
Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (back) remains out of action for Game 1 of Wednesday's doubleheader at Camden Yards against the division-rival Baltimore Orioles, per MLB.com. Sean Keys will make another start at first base and will bat fifth against Orioles right-hander Chris Bassitt. Guerrero is considered day-to-day right now in the final week of the regular season after departing Sunday's game early against the Texas Rangers due to tightness in his lower back. It is something that the 27-year-old Canadian slugger has already dealt with this year, and it could explain why the six-time All-Star has had a very disappointing 2026 campaign. Guerrero enters play on Wednesday with a .263/.336/.359 slash line, a .695 OPS, only nine home runs, 56 RBI, 71 runs scored, and seven steals across his 529 at-bats. Toronto entered play on Wednesday four games out of the final wild-card spot in the American League and on the brink of elimination. If they lose the first game of Wednesday's doubleheader, Guerrero could be shut down for the rest of the week.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com

The good news is that we’re less than a week from the end of this disappointing season. Anyway, here’s what’s happening around baseball. In Mariners news… - Eric Sanford wants to know what your favorite moments were from this godawful season. - Over on The Feed, commenter Jose Luis took a crack at outlining an offseason plan for the Mariners. Around the league… - The Red Sox have committed to
item.content:encoded:
Good morning folks!
The Mariners dropped another massive stinker in yesterday’s 7-0 loss to the Astros. The good news is that we’re less than a week from the end of this disappointing season.
Anyway, here’s what’s happening around baseball.
In Mariners news…
- Eric Sanford wants to know what your favorite moments were from this godawful season.
- Over on The Feed, commenter Jose Luis took a crack at outlining an offseason plan for the Mariners.
Around the league…
- The Red Sox have committed to keeping manager Chad Tracy and chief baseball officer Craig Breslow through at least 2029.
- The Mets have agreed to a three-year contract extension with manager Andy Green.
- The Yankees do not expect superstar outfielder Aaron Judge to be available during the Wild Card round.
- Michael Baumann at Fangraphs wonders if the Yanks have what it takes to be successful in the postseason without Judge in the lineup.
- The Cubs are not planning to place third baseman Alex Bregman on the injured list after he suffered multiple fractures in his face from a foul ball.
- The Rays have released former Mariners outfielder Jake Fraley.
- The Rockies became the fifth team in MLB history to have four straight seasons with 100+ losses.
- Paul Skenes blamed the World Baseball Classic for his declining velocity in 2026. As long as players continue to participate in the tournament I’m going to remain skeptical that they sincerely believe any of this.
- David Roth at Defector offered up a different theory: Team USA’s players are being punished for their redassery during the tournament.
- The MLB strike zone shrank a good deal in 2026, reports J.J. Cooper at Baseball America. ($)
- David Schoenfield at ESPN gave his regular season grades for all 30 clubs.
- Jeff Passan handed out his regular season superlatives high school yearbook style.
- Ryan Blake outlined the five biggest questions facing the sport in the run-up to the 2026 postseason.

El Oso Polar vive una temp
item.content:encoded:
El primera base de los Orioles está cerca de alcanzar un registro que no tiene registro desde hace más de un siglo en las Grandes Ligas
Pete Alonso está cerca de conseguir una marca inédita en la historia de las Grandes Ligas. El primera base de los Orioles de Baltimore tiene la oportunidad de convertirse en el primer jugador en más de un siglo de MLB que termina como líder de carreras impulsadas en ambas ligas, una estadística oficial que se tiene registro desde 1920.
El Oso Polar vive una temporada destacada con Baltimore y llega a la recta final del calendario como uno de los principales productores ofensivos de la Liga Americana. Su objetivo es completar una hazaña que ningún pelotero ha logrado desde la creación de las Grandes Ligas modernas.
La posibilidad de Alonso tiene como antecedente su rendimiento cuando formaba parte de la Liga Nacional. El toletero ya consiguió encabezar ese departamento en 2022 con los Mets de Nueva York y ahora busca repetir la hazaña del otro lado de la MLB con los Mets de Nueva York.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Justin Verlander prepara su última apertura en las Grandes Ligas
Alonso busca dominar las carreras impulsadas en ambas ligas
El reto de Pete Alonso está relacionado con su capacidad para producir carreras, una de las principales características que ha mostrado durante su trayectoria en las Grandes Ligas.
El primera base llegó a la temporada 2026 con una carrera consolidada como uno de los bateadores de mayor poder en MLB y ahora tiene la oportunidad de sumar un logro que ningún jugador ha alcanzado en 106 años de historia.
Durante su etapa anterior en la Liga Nacional, Alonso logró posicionarse como uno de los mejores productores ofensivos del circuito con 131 carreras impulsadas. Ahora, con los Orioles, busca repetir ese dominio en la Liga Americana.
De acuerdo con los registros históricos, ningún pelotero ha terminado una temporada como líder de carreras impulsadas en ambas ligas, por lo que Alonso podría convertirse en el primero en conseguirlo.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Alex Bregman recibe pelotazo en el rostro y abandona juego
Una temporada histórica con los Orioles
Pete Alonso llegó a Baltimore como una de las principales incorporaciones ofensivas del equipo y rápidamente asumió un papel importante dentro del orden al bate. El jugador ha mantenido su capacidad para generar extrabases y producir carreras, características que lo han acompañado desde su debut en MLB en 2019.
Además de su producción ofensiva, Alonso continúa ampliando su legado dentro del béisbol profesional. En 2026 también alcanzó una marca importante al llegar a los 300 cuadrangulares en su carrera, logro que consiguió como jugador de los Orioles frente a los Mets, su antiguo equipo.
Alonso busca entrar en la historia de MLB
La recta final de la temporada será determinante para conocer si Pete Alonso consigue completar una de las hazañas más difíciles del béisbol moderno. A menos de una semana de finalizar su primera temporada con los Orioles de Baltimore, Pete Alonso se mantiene en la pelea por una marca histórica. El primera base suma 108 carreras impulsadas, nueve más que el cubano Yordan Álvarez, quien acumula 99 y ocupa el segundo lugar de la Liga Americana en este departamento.
Con la recta final del calendario por disputarse, Alonso tiene una ventaja importante para quedarse con el liderato de impulsadas. Salvo que Álvarez tenga una última semana extraordinaria, el jugador de Baltimore podría terminar la campaña en la cima de este rubro y acercarse a una hazaña que no se consigue desde hace más de un siglo.
